title: Quasi-compact algebraic-space morphisms are closed in the constructible topology
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and point spaces with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact point space. A space is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. For a scheme, the constructible topology is locally the topology generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements on affine open charts. For an algebraic space, define its constructible topology to be the final topology for its representable etale affine scheme charts. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism between quasi-separated algebraic spaces. Then its map on constructible point spaces is closed: for every constructible-topology closed subset $F\subseteq|X|$, its image $|f|(F)\subseteq|Y|$ is closed in the constructible topology. No finite-type, finite-presentation, properness, or surjectivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Rydh Proposition (1.2)(ii), printed p.4, extended to algebraic spaces by Remark (1.8), printed pp.6--7; underlying scheme result EGA I, Proposition 7.2.12(iv). Author PDF https://davidrydh.se/papers/submersion20100305.pdf read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a constructible-closed $F\subseteq|X|$ and any representable etale affine chart $u:V\to Y$. Form $Z=X\times_YV$, with projections $r:Z\to X$ and $s:Z\to V$. By the definition of quasi-compactness of $f$, $|Z|$ is quasi-compact. The affine-atlas lemma gives a representable surjective etale map $h:W\to Z$ with $W$ affine. Put $a=rh:W\to X$ and $g=sh:W\to V$; then $fa=ug$.

source.place: Tag 03H6, lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover; fibre products: spaces.tex Tag 02X2, lemma-fibre-product-spaces. Rydh Remark (1.8), affine presentation reduction.

proof.text: The affine schemes $W,V$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence their Zariski point spaces are spectral. Consequently $|W|$ is quasi-compact in its constructible topology and $|V|$ is Hausdorff in its constructible topology. Here the scheme constructible topology is the patch topology of these spectral spaces.

source.place: Tag 0901, lemma-constructible-hausdorff-quasi-compact; properties.tex Tag 094L, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-spectral; algebra.tex Tag 00E8 and schemes.tex Tags 01KN, 01KO.

proof.text: Apply constructible-topology continuity to $a:W\to X$ and $g:W\to V$: $X$ is quasi-separated by hypothesis and $W,V$ are quasi-separated by step 2. Thus $C=|a|^{-1}(F)$ is constructible-closed in $|W|$, and $g$ is constructible-continuous. In particular $C$ is quasi-compact: lift an open cover of $C$ to opens of $|W|$ and adjoin the open complement of $C$; a finite subcover of $|W|$ restricts to one of $C$.

source.place: Proposition (1.2)(i) and Remark (1.8), printed pp.4,6--7; closed-subset argument explicitly as topology.tex Tag 005C, lemma-closed-in-quasi-compact.

proof.text: The continuous image $K=|g|(C)$ is quasi-compact in $|V|$ with the constructible topology. It is closed by the following elementary separation argument. For $v\notin K$, choose, for each $k\in K$, disjoint constructible-open neighborhoods $A_k$ of $k$ and $B_k$ of $v$, using the Hausdorff property from step 2. Finitely many $A_k$ cover $K$; the intersection of the corresponding $B_k$ is an open neighborhood of $v$ disjoint from $K$. This also works for $K=\varnothing$, using the empty intersection $|V|$. Hence the complement of $K$ is open.

source.place: Tag 04Z9, lemma-image-quasi-compact (1); the written finite-neighborhood argument is Tag 08YB, lemma-quasi-compact-in-Hausdorff (1), also used in Tag 0A2S, lemma-fibres-spectral-map-quasi-compact.

proof.text: We have $K=|u|^{-1}(|f|(F))$. One inclusion follows from $fa=ug$. Conversely, if $u(v)=f(x)$ with $x\in F$, point-surjectivity for fibre products gives $z\in|Z|$ mapping to $(x,v)$. Since $h$ is representable and surjective, its point map is surjective; choose $w\in|W|$ above $z$. Then $a(w)=x\in F$ and $g(w)=v$, so $v\in K$. For every affine etale chart of $Y$, the inverse image of $|f|(F)$ is therefore closed by step 4. By the defining final topology on $|Y|$, $|f|(F)$ is constructible-closed.

source.place: Tag 03H4, lemma-points-cartesian, and Tag 03H5, lemma-characterize-surjective; final-topology descent is Rydh Remark (1.8), printed pp.6--7.
